'''Mary C. Meyer''' is an American statistician. She is known for both theoretical and computational research in [[nonparametric statistics]] and [[density estimation]], especially for densities with shape constraints such as convexity or monotonicity.{{r|gmu}} She is a professor of statistics at [[Colorado State University]].{{r|colfac}}

==Education and career==
Meyer obtained her Ph.D. in 1996 from the [[University of Michigan]], under the supervision of [[Michael Woodroofe]]. Her [[thesis|dissertation]] was ''Shape-Restricted Inference with Applications to [[Nonparametric regression|Nonparametric Regression]], Smooth [[Nonparametric Estimation|Nonparametric Function Estimation]], and Density Estimation''.{{r|mg}} She was a faculty member in statistics at the [[University of Georgia]] before moving to Colorado State University.{{r|gmu}}

While a statistics professor at Colorado State University, Meyer declared that a study of salaries by CSU created salary goals for women faculty that were "[[Gender pay gap in the United States|substantially smaller than for men]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/news/2015/05/05/professor-csu-set-pay-goals-based-gender/26943335/|title=Professor: CSU study based pay goals on gender|first=Nick|last=Coltrain|website=The Coloradoan}}</ref>{{r|wage}} This led CSU to start studying pay equity in 2015, which in turn led later that year to a quarter of female full professors receiving higher pay.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/news/2017/11/19/csu-reports-its-closing-gender-pay-gap/863266001/|title=CSU reports it's closing gender pay gap|first=Nick|last=Coltrain|website=The Coloradoan}}</ref> She has also led faculty opposition to increases in athletic spending by the university.{{r|athletic}}

==Book==
Meyer is the author of the textbook ''Probability and Mathematical Statistics: Theory, Applications, and Practice in R'' (Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics, 2019).{{r|pms}}
